The main takeaway from our work is that

the Rocky Mountain foreland basin is a composite of many sedimentologically isolated basins of different ages that were created by Laramide basement deformation and that the Laramide foreland basin was a short-lived phenomenon of limited duration that was replaced by the post-Laramide foreland basins of Oligocene to Miocene age that are more familiar to most geologists.
the Laramide foreland basin was a complex system of interacting subbasins, each with its own history of tectonic and depositional events.
Laramide deformation and sedimentation in the central Rocky Mountains were not a single, coherent event, but rather a series of events that occurred in different basins at different times.
